Checking the options:

after replacing the symbols:

Applying the BODMAS rule, we will get,

Rightarrow 1.08 - **__6 × 27__** + 105 = 29

Rightarrow __**1.08**__ - 162 __**+ 105**__ = 29

Rightarrow __**106.08 - 162**__ = 29

= -55.92 ≠ 29.

 

**Option 2) ÷ and +**

after replacing the symbols:

Rightarrow 26 + __**24 ÷ 6**__ × 27 − 105 = 29

Applying the BODMAS rule, we will get,

Rightarrow 26 + __**4**____** × 27**__ − 105 = 29

Rightarrow __**26 + 108**__ - 105 = 29

Rightarrow **__134 - 105__** = 29

**= 29 = 29 True**

 

3) + and × 

after replacing the symbols:

Rightarrow 26 × 24 + __**6 ÷ 27**__ − 105 = 29

Applying the BODMAS rule, we will get,

Rightarrow __**26 ×**____** 24**__ + 0.22 − 105 = 29

Rightarrow __**624 + 0.22**__ − 105 = 29

Rightarrow __**624.22 - 105**__ = 29

= 519.22 ≠ 29.

 

4) ÷ and −

after replacing the symbols:

Rightarrow 26 - 24 + 6 × __**27 ÷ 105**__ = 29

Applying the BODMAS rule, we will get,

Rightarrow 26 - 24 + __**6 × 0.25**__ = 29

Rightarrow __**26**__ - 24 __**+ 1.5**__ = 29

Rightarrow **__27.5 - 24__** = 29

= 3.5 ≠ 29.

questions.question: The sum of a number and its reciprocal is 17/4, Find the numbers.
questions.solution:
Let the number be a.

According to question:

a + 1/a = 17/4

⇒ (a² + 1)/a = 17/4

⇒ 4(a² + 1) = 17a

⇒ 4a² + 4 = 17a

⇒ 4a² – 17a + 4 = 0

⇒ 4a² – (16 + 1)a + 4 = 0

⇒ 4a² – 16a – a + 4 = 0

⇒ 4a (a – 4) – 1(a – 4) = 0

⇒ (4a – 1) = 0 or (a – 4) = 0

⇒ a = 1/4 or a = 4

Hence, ‘4 and 1/4’ is the correct answer.

Given below are two statements labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R)

**Assertion (A): **The oldest paintings of Ajanta are datable to the second and first centuries B.C.

**Reason (R):** Chronologically the paintings of caves No. 1 and 2 are the last in the series and pertain to the Post-Gupta period

In the context of the above two statements which of the following is correct?

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution:
**Assertion**

 
• The earliest Ajanta caves were carved in the 2nd Century BC out of a horse-shoe-shaped cliffs along the Waghora River.
 
• They were used by Buddhist monks as prayer halls (chaitya grihas) and monasteries (viharas) for about nine centuries.

**REASON**

 
• Out of the 30 excavated caves, five (cave no. 9, 10, 19, 26, and 29) are chaitya grihas (prayer halls) and the rest are viharas (monasteries).
 
• In date and style, these caves can be divided into two broad phases.
 
• **Phase I (2nd Century to 1st Century BCE)** – The earliest excavations were done by the Satavahanas and belong to the Hinayana (Theravada) phase of Buddhism. The object of worship is a stupa here. Caves 9, 10, 12, 13 and 15A belong to this era.
 
• **Phase II (5th Century AD to 6th Century AD)** – These excavations are a major contribution of the Vakatakas and Chalukyas and belong to Mahayana phase of Buddhism which is mostly a Post Gupta age.

**Cave 1 **is a magnificently painted Vihara (monastery), filled with wall murals, sculptures, and ceiling paintings, that date back to the 5th century. Originally, Cave 1 also had a porch that led to the main hall, however, it has since collapsed.

**Cave 2** was started in the 460s but mostly carved between 475 and 477 CE, probably sponsored and influenced by a woman closely related to emperor Harisena. It has a porch quite different from Cave 1. Even the façade carvings seem to be different. The cave is supported by robust pillars, ornamented with designs. The front porch consists of cells supported by pillared vestibules on both ends.

questions.question:
Fill in the blanks by choosing the appropriate option.

Milk ........... Ensures that Vitamins (A/D) reach consumers who buy low-fat milk.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fortification**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Food Fortification: 

 
 
• Fortification is the addition of key vitamins and minerals such as Iron, Iodine, Zinc, Vitamins A & D to staple foods such as rice, wheat, oil, milk and salt to improve their nutritional content.
 
• These nutrients may or may not have been originally present in the food before processing or may have been lost during processing.
 
 
 
• Why do we Need the Fortification of Food?
 
 
• Deficiency of micronutrients or micronutrient malnutrition, also known as hidden hunger, is a serious health risk.
 
• Access to safe and nutritious food is a must and sometimes due to lack of consumption of a balanced diet, lack of variety in the diet or unavailability of food one does not get adequate micronutrients. Often, there is a considerable loss of nutrients during the processing of food as well.
 
• One of the strategies to address this problem is the fortification of food.
 
• This method complements other ways to improve nutrition such as diversification of diet and supplementation of food.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Standardization
 
 
 
• The adjustment of one or more of the milk constituents to meet the legal requirement or nominated level.
 
• In the market milk industry, normally involves reducing the butterfat content by the addition of skim milk or. Through the removal of the cream.
 
 
 
 

 Pasteurization
 
 
 
• Pasteurized milk is a raw milk that has been heated to a specified temperature and time to kill pathogens that may be found in the raw milk.
 
• Pathogens are microorganisms such as bacteria that make humans sick. Raw milk can contain pathogens such as Campylobacter, E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria, and other bacteria.
 
 
 
 

 Homogenization
 
 
 
• Homogenization is a mechanical process used to reduce the size of the fat globules in the milk.
 
• Reduce the milk fat globules size to less than 1.0 µm which allows them to stay evenly distributed in milk.
 
• Homogenization is a high-pressure process that forces milk at a high velocity through a small orifice to break up the globules.

questions.question: Which mountain range runs from northwest to southeast and forms a natural boundary between the Kashmir valley and the outer plains?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Pir Panjal Range is part of the Inner Himalayan region and runs from northwest to southeast, forming a natural boundary between the Kashmir Valley and the outer plains.
 
• This range separates the Kashmir Valley from the lesser Himalayan regions and lies south of the main Himalayan range.
 
• It is known for its significant mountain passes like the Pir Panjal Pass, Banihal Pass, and Rohtang Pass, which have been crucial for trade and travel.
 
• The range is home to dense forests and is rich in biodiversity, contributing significantly to the ecology of the region.
 
• The Pir Panjal Range is also known for its beautiful landscapes and is a popular destination for trekking and tourism in India.

• The Siachen Glacier, the largest glacier in India, is located in the Karakoram Range.

• It serves as a prominent tourist destination and is home to numerous trekking routes.

questions.question: A deficiency of which nutrient can lead to stunted growth and yellowing of leaves?
questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

**Role of Nitrogen in Plants**

__
 
• Nitrogen is a vital macronutrient for plants and plays a significant role in their growth and development.
 
• It is a major component of chlorophyll, which is essential for photosynthesis.
 
• Nitrogen is also a key element in amino acids, proteins, and nucleic acids, which are crucial for cell division and growth.

**EXPLANATION**__:

__
 
• A deficiency of nitrogen in plants can lead to:
 
 
• **Stunted Growth**: Since nitrogen is essential for cell division and elongation, a lack of it restricts growth.
 
• **Yellowing of Leaves**: Without sufficient nitrogen, chlorophyll production decreases, causing leaves to turn yellow, a condition known as chlorosis.
 
 
 
• Other options:
 
 
• **Calcium:** Deficiency affects cell wall structure but does not cause yellowing of leaves.
 
• **Phosphorus:** Deficiency leads to dark green or purplish leaves, not yellowing.
 
• **Potassium:** Deficiency causes browning of leaf edges, not stunted growth or yellowing.
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1: Nitrogen__.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and State legislatures is **correct**?

options.text: The State legislature can legislate on matters enumerated in the Union List
The Union legislature can legislate on matters in the Concurrent List only with State approval
The Union Government can issue directions to the States under Article 256
The Union and States have equal powers on matters in the Union List

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Union Government can issue directions to the States under Article 256**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 256 of the Indian Constitution states that the executive power of every state is to be exercised in a way that ensures compliance with the laws made by the Parliament.
 
• The Union Government has the authority to issue directions to the states to ensure the implementation of such laws.
 
• This provision ensures the supremacy of parliamentary laws over state laws in case of conflict.
 
• Such directions issued by the Union are binding on the states, and non-compliance may result in consequences under Article 356 (President’s Rule).
 
• This mechanism ensures the cohesive functioning of the federal structure in India and maintains the unity and integrity of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Legislature (Parliament)**

 
 
• Composition: President, Lok Sabha (House of the People), and Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• Powers: Exclusive power over Union List, concurrent power over Concurrent List, with overriding power over states.
 
• Rajya Sabha: Indirectly elected, permanent house (not dissolved), one-third members retire every two years, 12 nominated members for arts/science.
 
• Lok Sabha: Directly elected, represents the people. 
 
 
 
• **State Legislature**
 
 
• Composition: Varies; some bicameral (Assembly & Council), most unicameral (Assembly only).
 
• Powers: Exclusive power over State List, concurrent power over Concurrent List.
 
• Legislative Council (Upper House): Indirectly elected members from local authorities, graduates, teachers, MLAs, and nominated by Governor; permanent house, not dissolved, one-third retire every two years.
 
• Legislative Assembly (Lower House): Directly elected by people, members 40-500.

questions.question: Distribution of Taxes between Centre and States in India is done by the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Finance Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Finance Commission** of India is a constitutional body established under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is responsible for the **distribution of financial resources** between the Centre and the States, primarily the division of tax revenues.
 
• The Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India every five years or as deemed necessary.
 
• The recommendations of the Finance Commission are **advisory in nature**, but they carry significant weight in determining fiscal allocations.
 
• The **15th Finance Commission**, chaired by N.K. Singh, submitted its report for the period 2021-26.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is established under **Article 280** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It recommends the **principles of tax-sharing** between the Centre and States and provides grants-in-aid to states in need of assistance.
 
 
 
• **Composition:**
 
 
• The Finance Commission consists of a Chairperson and four other members, who are appointed by the President of India.
 
• The qualifications and selection criteria are determined by the Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Functions:**
 
 
• It decides the **distribution of net proceeds of taxes** between the Centre and States.
 
• It also determines the principles governing grants-in-aid to states from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
• It addresses issues related to augmenting the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The recommendations of the Finance Commission ensure **equitable fiscal federalism** and address regional imbalances in development.
 
• It facilitates the smooth functioning of the fiscal framework in India.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Aalmi Tablighi Ijtema :

1) It is cited as the world's second-largest Islamic gathering.

2) It is organized by the Tablighi Jamaat, focusing on spiritual reflection.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Only 2.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **Aalmi Tablighi Ijtema** in **Bhopal** is a massive, annual international Islamic gathering (congregation) organized by the **Tablighi Jamaat,** focusing on spiritual reflection.
 
• It is often cited as the **world's third-largest Islamic** gathering, following the Hajj in Mecca and the Bishwa Ijtima in Bangladesh.
 
• **Location:** Historically held at Taj-ul-Masajid in Bhopal, it was moved to Eintkhedi (Ghasipura) in 2005 due to massive crowds.
 
• **Nature**: The event is strictly spiritual and non-political. It focuses on the "Six Principles" of the Tablighi Jamaat, aiming for self-reformation and the revival of Islamic faith.
 
• **Origin**: The first Ijtima in Bhopal was held in 1944 (some sources cite 1948 or 1949) at Masjid Shakoor Khan, attended by only 14 people.
 
• **Growth**: It has grown into a global phenomenon, with recent attendance exceeding 1 to 1.2 million people from over 50 countries.
 
• **Duration:** Traditionally a three-day event (Saturday to Monday), it has recently expanded to four days (Friday to Monday).
 
• **Mass Marriages (Nikahs)**: A notable feature is the performance of hundreds of simplified, low-cost mass marriages following Islamic traditions to discourage ostentation.
 
• **Dua-e-Khas:** The event concludes with a grand collective prayer (Dua) for global peace and prosperity.
 
• **Community Management:** The gathering is unique for its self-sustained management by over 25,000 volunteers who handle everything from sanitation to security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Socio-Religious Impact of Tablighi Jamaat:**

 
• **Internal Reformation:** Unlike political groups, it focuses on orthopraxy (correct practice) rather than orthodoxy. It emphasizes "Iman" (faith) and "Akhlaq" (morals).
 
• **Simplicity & De-escalation:** The Ijtima promotes frugality (as seen in the mass marriages/Nikahs) to counter the social burden of expensive weddings in the community.
 
• **Non-Political Stance**: By strictly avoiding political debates, it maintains a unique space in India's secular fabric, though it often faces administrative scrutiny during international health crises or security checks.
 
• **Global Networking**: It creates a "Global Muslim Identity" that transcends national borders, facilitating cultural exchange among delegates from the Middle East, Africa, and SE Asia.

questions.question: Which geographical feature significantly contributed to the prosperity of Mahajanapadas during the Vedic period?
questions.solution: The prosperity of Mahajanapadas during the Vedic period was largely due to their location in fertile river valleys, such as those of the Ganges and Yamuna. These valleys provided rich alluvial soil, which supported agriculture and enabled large populations to thrive. The agricultural surplus facilitated trade and commerce, contributing to the economic strength of these kingdoms. In contrast, coastal plains and desert regions lacked the same agricultural potential, while mountain ranges posed challenges for settlement and trade. Thus, river valleys were pivotal in the development and prosperity of Mahajanapadas.

questions.question: From 11 to 50, how many numbers are there which are exactly divisible by 7 but not by 3?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total multiples of 7 from 11 to 50 = (Largest multiple − Smallest multiple) ÷ 7 + 1 = (49 − 14) ÷ 7 + 1 = 6.

Total multiples of 21 (divisible by both 7 and 3) from 11 to 50 = (42 − 21) ÷ 21 + 1 = 2.

Total numbers divisible by 7 but not by 3 = 6 − 2 = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 numbers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Range of numbers: From 11 to 50.

Condition: Numbers must be divisible by 7 but not by 3.

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, list all the numbers between 11 and 50 that are exactly divisible by 7.

⇒ These multiples are: 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49.

⇒ Total count of these multiples = 6.

⇒ Next, identify the numbers from this list that are also divisible by 3.

⇒ A number divisible by both 7 and 3 must be divisible by their LCM, which is 21.

⇒ The multiples of 21 in the given range are: 21 and 42.

⇒ We must exclude these 2 numbers from our initial list.

⇒ The remaining numbers are: 14, 28, 35, 49.

⇒ Total count of the remaining numbers = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 numbers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM of Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime (like 3 and 7, having no common factors other than 1), their Least Common Multiple (LCM) is simply their product (3 × 7 = 21). Any number divisible by both must be a multiple of this LCM.

Arithmetic Progression (AP) Counting

To find the number of terms in an AP, you can use the formula: Number of terms = (Last term − First term) ÷ Common Difference + 1.

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is exactly divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3.
</p

questions.question: Find a number such that when 15 is subtracted from 7 times the number, the result is 10 more than twice the number
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For word problems involving equations, verifying the given options is the fastest approach.

Let us check Option 1: The number is 5.

Left Side (15 subtracted from 7 times) → 7 × 5 − 15 = 35 − 15 = 20.

Right Side (10 more than twice) → 2 × 5 + 10 = 10 + 10 = 20.

Since both sides match perfectly (20 = 20), this is the required number.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

When 15 is subtracted from 7 times a number, the result is equal to 10 more than twice the same number.

**Formula Used:**

Forming a basic linear equation in one variable: ax + b = cx + d

**Calculations:**

Let the required number be x.

⇒ 15 subtracted from 7 times the number = 7x − 15

⇒ 10 more than twice the number = 2x + 10

According to the given question, we equate both expressions:

⇒ 7x − 15 = 2x + 10

⇒ 7x − 2x = 10 + 15

⇒ 5x = 25

⇒ x = 25 ÷ 5

⇒ x = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Linear Equation in One Variable

An equation of the form ax + b = 0, where a and b are constant values and x is a variable, is called a linear equation. It always yields a single unique solution.

Translating Word Problems to Algebra

Key phrases like 'times' refer to multiplication, 'more than' refers to addition, and 'subtracted from' means taking away from a base value (e.g., '15 subtracted from y' translates directly to y − 15).

Checking the Solution

Always verify the final algebraic answer by substituting the value back into both sides of the original word problem to ensure the Left Hand Side (LHS) strictly equals the Right Hand Side (RHS).
</p

questions.question: From a point P on a level ground, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 30°. If the tower is 100 m high, the distance of point P from the foot of the tower is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a 30°-60°-90° right-angled triangle, the sides opposite these angles are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2.

The height of the tower is opposite to the 30° angle → 1 unit = 100 m.

The base distance is opposite to the 60° angle → √3 units.

Distance = 100 × √3 = 100 × 1.732 = 173.2 m ≈ 173 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 173 metre.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1713bf4dcf3d17c6dc4a539555a76f2dd89b9c1090e91f25c658c7146d8ae61c.png] 

**Given:**

Height of the tower AB (h) = 100 m

Angle of elevation of the top from point P (θ) = 30°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculation:**

Let the distance of point P from the foot of the tower (BP) be x.

In the right-angled triangle ABP:

⇒ tan 30° = AB ÷ BP

⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = 100 ÷ x

⇒ x = 100 × √3

⇒ x = 100 × 1.732

⇒ x = 173.2 m

⇒ x ≈ 173 m

**∴ The correct answer is 173 metre.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation vs Angle of Depression

The angle of elevation is measured upwards from the horizontal line of sight to an object. The angle of depression is measured downwards. Due to alternate interior angles, the angle of elevation of a point A from B is exactly equal to the angle of depression of B from A.

30°-60°-90° Triangle Rule

In any right-angled triangle with acute angles of 30° and 60°, the side lengths opposite the 30°, 60°, and 90° angles are always in the constant ratio of 1 : √3 : 2. This rule allows for rapid problem-solving without the need for extensive trigonometric calculations.

45°-45°-90° Triangle Rule

If the angle of elevation is 45°, an isosceles right-angled triangle is formed. In this case, the perpendicular height is exactly equal to the base distance, and the sides maintain a ratio of 1 : 1 : √2.
</p

questions.question: The length of a room is 5.5 m and the width is 3.75 m. Find the cost of paving the floor with slabs at the rate of Rs. 800 per sq. meter.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Cost = Length × Width × Rate per m²

Cost = 5.5 × 3.75 × 800

Multiply 3.75 by 800 first: 3.75 × 800 = 3000

Cost = 5.5 × 3000 = 16500

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 16500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7ab45d720effbf3d98a32c6c6fd3a7c8d3a062645544ab5a7d1989215aebe228.png] 

**Given:**

Length of the room (L) = 5.5 m

Width of the room (W) = 3.75 m

Rate of paving = Rs. 800 per m²

**Formula Used:**

Area of a rectangle = Length × Width

Total Cost = Area × Rate per unit area

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of the floor = 5.5 m × 3.75 m

⇒ Area = 20.625 m²

⇒ Total Cost = 20.625 × 800

⇒ Total Cost = 16500

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 16500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The total space enclosed within the boundaries of a rectangle. Formula: Area = Length × Breadth.

Perimeter of Rectangle

The total length of the boundary of a rectangle. Formula: Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Breadth). This is used for finding the cost of fencing or placing borders.

Area of Square

A square is a special type of rectangle where all four sides are equal. Formula: Area = Side².
</p

questions.question: Rohan sells an umbrella to Bhima at a profit of 25%. Bhima sells the same to Sambhu at a profit of 20%.Sambhu sells it to Dharmendra at ₹5,400, thereby earning a profit of 20%. Find the cost price to Rohan.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial cost price to Rohan be x. We use the multiplying factor method for successive profits.

x × 1.25 × 1.20 × 1.20 = 5400

x × (5/4) × (6/5) × (6/5) = 5400

x × (9/5) = 5400 ⇒ x = 3000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit earned by Rohan = 25%

Profit earned by Bhima = 20%

Profit earned by Sambhu = 20%

Selling Price to Dharmendra = ₹5,400

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + Profit% ÷ 100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5309fb00a71cd9bcb96cee4494f7ab9fa1522856cb56dc203d0a6d216fefe09a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost price for Rohan be x.

⇒ Selling price for Rohan = x × (100 + 25)/100 = x × 125/100 = 5x/4

⇒ Cost price for Bhima is 5x/4.

⇒ Selling price for Bhima = (5x/4) × (100 + 20)/100 = (5x/4) × 120/100 = (5x/4) × (6/5) = 3x/2

⇒ Cost price for Sambhu is 3x/2.

⇒ Selling price for Sambhu = (3x/2) × (100 + 20)/100 = (3x/2) × 120/100 = (3x/2) × (6/5) = 9x/5

⇒ Since Sambhu sells to Dharmendra for ₹5,400:

⇒ 9x/5 = 5400

⇒ x = 5400 × (5/9)

⇒ x = 600 × 5 = 3000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

If an item undergoes successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the effective percentage change is given by (a + b + (a × b)/100)%.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP). The Selling Price (SP) can be calculated as SP = MP × (1 − Discount% ÷ 100).

Base of Profit / Loss Calculation

Unless otherwise explicitly stated, profit or loss percentage is always calculated on the initial Cost Price (CP). Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.question: The present population of a city is 17,500. The population decreases by 12% in the first year and increases by 8% in the second year. Find the population after 2 years.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the successive multiplying factor method for consecutive percentage changes:

Final Population = Initial Population × (1 − Decrease%) × (1 + Increase%)

Final Population = 17500 × (88 ÷ 100) × (108 ÷ 100)

Final Population = 17500 × 0.88 × 1.08 = 15400 × 1.08 = 16632

**∴ The correct answer is 16,632.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Initial population of the city = 17500

⇒ First year percentage change = −12% (Decrease)

⇒ Second year percentage change = +8% (Increase)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/058528c1e8e1da6bdb904c81caec5a01a58c3a7c79e79c137a60d12450683732.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± R₁ ÷ 100) × (1 ± R₂ ÷ 100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Population after the first year = 17500 × (1 − 12 ÷ 100)

⇒ Population after the first year = 17500 × 0.88 = 15400

⇒ Population after the second year = 15400 × (1 + 8 ÷ 100)

⇒ Population after the second year = 15400 × 1.08 = 16632

**∴ The correct answer is 16,632.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes multiple percentage changes in succession, the net percentage change can be computed as: Net Change = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100.

Multiplying Factor Method

The most efficient way to compute final base values is by applying fraction multipliers: (1 + x ÷ 100) for an increase and (1 − x ÷ 100) for a decrease.

Base Change Principle

In consecutive changes, the new percentage operation always applies to the newly formed base (the result of the previous year), not the original starting base.
</p

questions.question: Find the ratio between the fourth proportional of 8, 9, 15 and the fourth proportional of 12, 18, 20.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The fourth proportional of three numbers a, b, c is calculated as (b × c) ÷ a.

Fourth proportional of 8, 9, 15 = (9 × 15) ÷ 8 = 135 / 8.

Fourth proportional of 12, 18, 20 = (18 × 20) ÷ 12 = 30.

Required Ratio = (135 / 8) : 30 = 135 : 240 = 9 : 16.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First set of numbers: 8, 9, 15

Second set of numbers: 12, 18, 20

**Formula Used:**

For any four numbers in proportion a : b :: c : d, the relationship is a / b = c / d.

⇒ The fourth proportional d = (b × c) / a.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/84a39d9093f4aafe52c76fadf9ff0ceabe9614a22dc43a65c6853cba9567514b.png] 

**Calculation:**

Let the fourth proportional of the first set be x.

⇒ 8 / 9 = 15 / x

⇒ x = (9 × 15) / 8

⇒ x = 135 / 8

Let the fourth proportional of the second set be y.

⇒ 12 / 18 = 20 / y

⇒ y = (18 × 20) / 12

⇒ y = 360 / 12

⇒ y = 30

Now, the ratio of x to y is:

⇒ Ratio = (135 / 8) : 30

⇒ Ratio = 135 : (30 × 8)

⇒ Ratio = 135 : 240

Dividing both sides by 15:

⇒ Ratio = 9 : 16

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two positive numbers a and b is √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion (a : b :: b : c), then c is the third proportional, computed directly as c = b² ÷ a.

Duplicate and Sub-duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a : b is given as a² : b², while its sub-duplicate ratio is expressed as √a : √b.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio formed by two separate ratios a : b and c : d is calculated by multiplying the antecedents together and consequents together, resulting in (a × c) : (b × d).
</p

questions.question: A solid wooden toy is in the shape of a right circular cone mounted on a hemisphere. If the radius of the hemisphere is 5.6 cm and the total height of the toy is 11.6 cm, then what is the volume of the wooden toy (in cm3 ) (rounded off to the closest integral value)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the combined volume formula for a cone on a hemisphere: V = (1/3) × π × r² × (2r + h)

Cone height h = Total height − radius = 11.6 − 5.6 = 6 cm.

V = (1/3) × (22/7) × 5.6 × 5.6 × (2 × 5.6 + 6)

V = (1/3) × 22 × 0.8 × 5.6 × 17.2 ≈ 565.07 cm³

Rounding off to the closest integer gives 565 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 565 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b450a9f57f3a9424c8d527d9eeff52a8b005ab2ac9e1b3a07457a94c7ebd2147.png] 

**Given:**

Total height of the toy = 11.6 cm

Radius of hemisphere (r) = 5.6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a Cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h

Volume of a Hemisphere = (2/3) × π × r³

Total Volume = (1/3) × π × r² × (2r + h)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Height of cone (h) = Total height − Radius of hemisphere

⇒ h = 11.6 − 5.6 = 6 cm

⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × (5.6)² × (2 × 5.6 + 6)

⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 31.36 × (11.2 + 6)

⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × 22 × 4.48 × 17.2

⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × 98.56 × 17.2

⇒ Total Volume = 1695.232 ÷ 3 ≈ 565.07 cm³

⇒ Rounding to the closest integral value, the volume is 565 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 565 cm³.**

questions.question: Two trains start at the same time from stations P and Q, 1800 km apart, and proceed towards each other at an average speed of 108 km/h and 92km/h, respectively. The trains will meet at:

Total distance between station P and Q = 1800 km

Speed of train from station P = 108 km/h

Speed of train from station Q = 92 km/h

Relative Speed (in opposite directions) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is calculated as the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Proportionality of Distance and Speed

When the time of travel is constant (e.g. when objects start moving at the exact same time), the distance covered is directly proportional to their speeds. Hence, D₁ ÷ D₂ = S₁ ÷ S₂.

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies travel in the same direction, the relative speed is obtained by taking the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂).

questions.question: If (y²-1)/(y)=6, then the value of (y⁶-1)/(y³) will be:

questions.question: In ∆ABC, ∠B = 90° and BD ⟂ AC. If AC = 9 cm and AD = 3 cm, then BD is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

By the Geometric Mean Theorem for a right-angled triangle:

Altitude to hypotenuse = √(Product of hypotenuse segments)

CD = AC − AD = 9 − 3 = 6 cm

BD = √(3 × 6) = √18 = 3√2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 3√2 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In right-angled ΔABC, ∠B = 90°

BD ⊥ AC

AC = 9 cm, AD = 3 cm

**Formula Used:**

In a right triangle, when an altitude is drawn from the right angle to the hypotenuse, the square of the altitude equals the product of the lengths of the two segments on the hypotenuse: BD² = AD × DC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/daaaf049f5d8ba63677e68665bb1ea5f98a0bfb2e62df759bba5757e9ce0e137.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ DC = AC − AD

⇒ DC = 9 − 3 = 6 cm

⇒ BD² = AD × DC

⇒ BD² = 3 × 6

⇒ BD² = 18

⇒ BD = √18 = 3√2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 3√2 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Geometric Mean Theorem (Altitude Rule)

In a right-angled triangle, the altitude drawn to the hypotenuse divides it into two segments such that the altitude is the geometric mean of these two segments. (Altitude² = Segment 1 × Segment 2)

Leg Rule of a Right Triangle

Each leg of a right-angled triangle is the geometric mean of the hypotenuse and the segment of the hypotenuse adjacent to that leg. (Leg² = Hypotenuse × Adjacent Segment)

Pythagorean Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two legs. (H² = P² + B²)
</p

questions.question: A and B together completed a piece of work costing Rs. 1,900. A worked for 5 days, B for 6 days. If the daily wages of A and B are in the ratio of 4 : 3 respectively, then how much amount will be received by A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total wage ratio = (A's days × A's daily wage) : (B's days × B's daily wage)

Wage ratio of A and B = (5 × 4) : (6 × 3) = 20 : 18 = 10 : 9

Total units = 10 + 9 = 19 units

Amount received by A = (10 ÷ 19) × 1900 = Rs. 1000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total cost of work = Rs. 1,900

Time taken by A = 5 days

Time taken by B = 6 days

Ratio of daily wages of A and B = 4 : 3

**Formula Used:**

Total Wage = Number of days worked × Daily wage rate

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fcbf15613f2a003f45c01dad2ffc0ecf5cfb29100aef6b111723dc4ebf52ae00.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the daily wages of A and B be 4x and 3x respectively.

⇒ Total wage earned by A = 5 × 4x = 20x

⇒ Total wage earned by B = 6 × 3x = 18x

⇒ Sum of total wages = 20x + 18x = 38x

⇒ 38x = 1900

⇒ x = 1900 ÷ 38 = 50

⇒ Amount received by A = 20x = 20 × 50 = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages Distribution

Wages are always distributed in direct proportion to the amount of total work done by each individual.

Equal Work Duration

If individuals work for the same number of days, their wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies or daily wages.

Partnership Analogy

Similar to a partnership where Profit = Capital × Time, in wage distribution, Total Wage = Daily Rate × Time Worked.
</p

questions.question: Aman's average score in a series of tests was ‘y’. He appeared in one more test and obtained score ‘z’. If Aman appeared in total ‘n’ tests, then which one of the following expression shows his average score for all the tests?

Total number of tests taken by Aman = n.

Number of initial tests before the last one = n − 1.

Total sum of all n tests = Initial sum + Score of last test = y(n − 1) + z.

New Average = Total Sum ÷ Total Tests = [y(n − 1) + z] / n.

**∴ The correct answer is [y(n − 1) + z] / n.**

**Given:**

Total number of tests appeared = n

Average score in the series before the last test = y

Score obtained in the last test = z

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of Observations ÷ Nu

When coefficients of variables are swapped, subtract the smaller equation from the larger one to find the difference directly.

⇒ F − S = 28

**∴ The correct answer is 28 years.**

⇒ 2F + 4S = 182 --- (Equation 3)

questions.question: The length and the breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 3 : 2. If the area of the field is 3456 m² , then what is the cost of fencing the field at the rate of Rs.3.50 per m?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let length = 3x and breadth = 2x. Area = 6x² = 3456 ⇒ x = 24.

Perimeter = 2 × (3x + 2x) = 10x.

Total cost = Perimeter × Rate = 10x × 3.50 = 35x.

Total cost = 35 × 24 = Rs. 840.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 840.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of length to breadth = 3 : 2

Area of rectangular field = 3456 m²

Cost of fencing = Rs. 3.50 per m

**Formula Used:**

Area of Rectangle = Length × Breadth

Perimeter of Rectangle = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

Total Cost = Perimeter × Rate

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dbe885e6fd773d57af5a73435e6fe5a1542f4328c2e164cf7325582a690e4074.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the length be 3x and the breadth be 2x.

⇒ Area = 3x × 2x = 6x²

⇒ 6x² = 3456

⇒ x² = 3456 ÷ 6

⇒ x² = 576

⇒ x = √576 = 24 m

⇒ Length = 3 × 24 = 72 m

⇒ Breadth = 2 × 24 = 48 m

⇒ Perimeter of the rectangular field = 2 × (72 + 48)

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × 120 = 240 m

⇒ Cost of fencing = Perimeter × Rate per m

⇒ Cost of fencing = 240 × 3.50 = Rs. 840

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 840.**

**__Additional Information__**

Area and Perimeter of Rectangle

Area represents the total space enclosed by the rectangle, calculated as Length × Breadth. Perimeter represents the total boundary length, calculated as 2 × (Length + Breadth).

Cost of Fencing vs Cost of Flooring

Fencing forms an outline along the boundary, so its cost relies entirely on the Perimeter × Rate. Flooring or tiling covers the interior surface, making its cost equal to Area × Rate.

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The length of the longest pole that can be placed straight within a rectangular room or field is its diagonal, given by the Pythagorean property: √(Length² + Breadth²).
</p

questions.question: Pabitra takes twice as long as Kader or three times as long as Rahim to complete a task. If they work together, they can complete the task in 2 days. How long will it take Kader to complete the task on his own?

Perimeter = 4 × Side = 4 × (4x + 2) = 16x + 8

**∴ The correct answer is 16x + 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the square = 16x² + 16x + 4

**Formula Used:**

Area of square = a²

Perimeter of square = 4a (where a is the side of the square)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc668ef6d4fb1c0f4e3d9cb47583c66456ca3b2963e80b49f11091d7c69b0feb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ a² = 16x² + 16x + 4

⇒ a² = 4(4x² + 4x + 1)

⇒ a² = 4(2x + 1)²

⇒ a = √[4(2x + 1)²]

⇒ a = 2(2x + 1) = 4x + 2

⇒ Perimeter = 4a

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × (4x + 2)

⇒ Perimeter = 16x + 8

**∴ The correct answer is 16x + 8.**

Diagonal of a Square

The length of the diagonal of a square with side a is given by d = a√2.

Algebraic Identity Used

The identity (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² is fundamental in factorising perfect square quadratic expressions.

Area of Square from Diagonal

The area can also be directly calculated if the diagonal d is known, using the formula Area = d² ÷ 2.
